history.period: DATE CONFLICT: 11th-12th century AD per xploreall; late 13th century AD per the AP Archaeology Department's Khammam district note (stylistic/inscriptional grounds)
history.summary: The Sri Ganapeshwaralayam at Kusumanchi, a Kakatiya-era Shiva temple about 20-22 km north of Khammam town, famed for one of South India's largest Shivalingams (DIMENSION CONFLICT: The Hindu reports ~3 m height with 2 m radius; xploreall reports 6 ft high — flagged). The temple has a high adhistana with a single east-facing shrine, antarala and pillared rangamandapa (the mandapa now ruined/missing), an adhistana frieze of elephants and hamsa motifs, and a star-shaped base said to mirror the linga shape; local lore holds it was built by the Kakatiya king Ganapati (xploreall's 'Lord Ganapati' presumably means Ganapatideva) and that an armless, legless sculptor stacked the huge stones, and the shrine is aligned so the sunrise rays fall on the lingam daily. The temple lay buried under scrub and mounds for centuries until it was brought to light through the initiative of the then Kusumanchi CI Sathu Weerapratap Reddy with villagers, after which worship resumed and the shrine grew as a pilgrimage centre. The Archaeology Department dates it to the late 13th century AD on stylistic and inscriptional grounds and had proposed Rs. 30 lakh of conservation works. CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV town 'Khammam' is imprecise — the temple is at Kusumanchi (a town and mandal headquarters), ~20-22 km from Khammam town; corrected to Kusumanchi. District (Khammam) and state (Telangana) are correct.

name: Sri Ganapeshwaralayam (Kusumanchi)
town_description: Kusumanchi is a town and mandal headquarters in Khammam district, Telangana, about 20-22 km north of Khammam town. It is best known for the Kakatiya-era Ganapeshwaralayam Shiva temple with one of South India's largest Shivalingams, a major Shivaratri pilgrimage site.
